* **Data setup**: SDA must be stable _before_ SCL rises
* **Data valid**: SDA remains stable _while_ SCL is high
* **Data hold**: SDA may change _after_ SCL falls

The FSM samples `ctrl_sda_i` on `scl_i_posedge` (SCL rising edge) to capture data during the valid window.

**Timing Impact:**

The 2-cycle synchronizer delay means:

* External SDA transition → 2 cycles later → `ctrl_sda_i` reflects change
* External SCL transition → 2 cycles later → `ctrl_scl_i` reflects change
* `scl_i_posedge` detection adds 1 more cycle → total 3-cycle latency

This delay is accounted for in timing calculations (embedded in `t_r_i`, `t_f_i` parameters).

=== 5.4 OD vs PP Mode Selection

**Mode Selection Logic** (line 336):

[source,systemverilog]
----
assign internal_sel_od_pp = ~tx_is_addr_i && (!ibi_address_byte_i);
----

**Truth Table:**

[cols="2,2,1,2,3", options="header"]
|===
| Operation | `tx_is_addr_i` | `ibi_address_byte_i` | `internal_sel_od_pp` | Mode & Rationale

| **Address byte TX**
| 1
| X (don't care)
| 0
| **OD**: Address phase always uses open-drain per I3C spec. Allows target ACK via open-drain pull-down.

| **IBI broadcast 8'h7E**
| 0
| 1
| 0
| **OD**: Broadcast address uses open-drain. IBI detection relies on bus collision (target pulls SDA).

| **Data byte TX/RX**
| 0
| 0
| 1
| **PP**: I3C data phase uses push-pull for higher speed (up to 12.5 MHz typical SDR).

| **START/STOP/repeated START**
| X
| X
| 0 (forced)
| **OD**: Bus conditions always use open-drain to ensure compatibility and proper timing.
|===

**Timing Profile Switching:**

When `internal_sel_od_pp` changes, the timing counter automatically selects the appropriate formula:

[source,systemverilog]
----
// Lines 112-142:
if (internal_sel_od_pp == 1'b0) begin
  // OD mode timing
  tSetupStart: tcount_d = t_r_i + tsu_sta_i;
  tClockLow:   tcount_d = tlow_i - thd_dat_i;
  // ...
end else begin
  // PP mode timing
  tSetupStart: tcount_d = t_r_pp_i + t_cbsr_i;
  tClockLow:   tcount_d = tlow_pp_i - thd_pp_i;
  // ...
end
----

**Mode Transition Example:**

[cols="1,2,2,2", options="header"]
|===
| Byte # | Operation | Mode | Timing Used

| 1 | Address 0x3C (write)
| OD (`internal_sel_od_pp = 0`)
| `t_r_i`, `tlow_i`, `thigh_i`, etc.

| 2 | Data 0xAB
| PP (`internal_sel_od_pp = 1`)
| `t_r_pp_i`, `tlow_pp_i`, `thigh_pp_i`, etc.

| 3 | Data 0xCD
| PP
| `t_r_pp_i`, `tlow_pp_i`, `thigh_pp_i`, etc.

| — | STOP condition
| OD (forced)
| `t_r_i`, `tsu_sto_i`, `t_buf_i`
|===

The mode switch is atomic (occurs during `load_tcount` in state transitions), preventing glitches or incorrect timing mid-byte.

'''

== Section 6: Signal Control Logic

This section documents how the FSM controls SCL and SDA outputs in each state.

=== 6.1 SCL Output Generation

The `scl_d` signal controls the SCL line (0 = pull low, 1 = release high). The following table shows SCL control by state:

[cols="2,1,4", options="header"]
|===
| State(s) | SCL Value | Purpose

| **Idle**
| 1 (high) unless `rx_req_i=1` then 0
| Bus idle (both lines released) or prepare for RX

| **Active**
| 1 if `tx_start_stop_i == Start`, else 0
| Setup for START (SCL high) or continue clock (SCL low)

| **SetupStart**
| 1 (high)
| Both lines released before START condition

| **HoldStart**
| 1 (high)
| SCL remains high while SDA falls (START)

| **ClockStart**
| 0 (low)
| Pull SCL low after START, enter clock cycle

| **ClockLow** (TX/RX)
| 0 (low)
| SCL low phase, data setup time

| **ClockPulse** (TX/RX)
| 1 (high)
| SCL high phase, data valid/sample time

| **HoldBit** (TX/RX)
| 0 (low)
| SCL low after pulse, data hold time

| **AckLow** / **ReadTbitLow**
| 0 (low)
| 9th bit low phase, setup ACK/T-bit

| **AckPulse** / **ReadTbitPulse**
| 1 (high)
| 9th bit high phase, sample ACK/T-bit

| **AckHold** / **ReadTbitHold**
| 0 (low)
| 9th bit hold, byte complete

| **SetupStop**
| 0 (low)
| SCL low before STOP condition

| **RiseStop**
| 1 (high)
| SCL rises for STOP condition

| **HoldStop**
| 1 (high)
| SCL remains high during bus free time

| **FetchTxData**
| 0 (low)
| Maintain clock low during data load
|===

**Clock Cycle Pattern** (for data bits):

[source]
----
ClockLow → ClockPulse → HoldBit → (repeat 8 times)
   SCL=0      SCL=1       SCL=0

Timeline:
   ____      ___      ____      ___
SCL    \____/   \____/    \____/   \____  (repeats 8x for 8 bits)
       |    |   |    |    |    |
     Setup Valid Hold Setup Valid Hold ...
       (tClockLow)  (tClockPulse)  (tHoldBit)
----

=== 6.2 SDA Output Generation

The `sda_d` signal controls the SDA line (0 = pull low, 1 = release high or drive high in PP mode). SDA control is more complex, depending on state and operational context:

==== 6.2.1 SDA Control by State (TX Mode)

[cols="2,1,3", options="header"]
|===
| State | SDA Value | Notes

| **Idle**
| 1 (released)
| Bus idle condition

| **Active**
| `sda_q` (previous)
| Hold previous value to avoid glitches

| **SetupStart**
| 1 (released)
| Both lines high before START

| **HoldStart**
| 0 (pull low)
| SDA falls while SCL high = START

| **ClockStart**
| 0 (remains low)
| SDA low after START

| **ClockLow**
| `shift_reg[bit_index]` or 1 (if repeated START)
| Data bit transmission

| **ClockPulse**
| `shift_reg[bit_index]`
| Data bit stable during SCL high

| **HoldBit**
| `shift_reg[bit_index]`
| Data bit hold after SCL falls

| **AckLow** (address byte)
| 1 (released)
| Release for target ACK

| **AckLow** (T-bit)
| `!(^shift_reg)`
| Drive T-bit (odd parity)

| **AckLow** (IBI acceptance)
| 0 (ACK) or 1 (NACK)
| Controller decides IBI acceptance

| **AckPulse**
| Same as AckLow
| Maintain SDA during SCL high

| **AckHold**
| 1 (released)
| Release SDA after ACK

| **SetupStop**
| 0 (pull low)
| SDA low before STOP

| **RiseStop**
| 0 (remains low)
| SDA low while SCL rises

| **HoldStop**
| 1 (released)
| SDA rises while SCL high = STOP

| **FetchTxData**
| Previous value
| No SDA change during load
|===

==== 6.2.2 SDA Control by State (RX Mode)

[cols="2,1,3", options="header"]
|===
| State | SDA Value | Notes

| **ReadClockLow**
| 1 (released)
| Release SDA for target to drive

| **ReadClockPulse**
| 1 (released)
| Target drives SDA, controller samples

| **ReadHoldBit**
| 1 (released)
| Release SDA, target may change data

| **ReadTbitLow**
| 1 (released)
| Release SDA for target T-bit

| **ReadTbitPulse**
| 1 (released) or 0 (if `abort_read_i`)
| Sample T-bit, or drive low to abort

| **ReadTbitHold**
| 1 (released) or 0 (if abort)
| Maintain SDA based on abort decision
|===

==== 6.2.3 SDA Control Logic (Code Implementation)

Key sections from `state_outputs` block (lines 323-555):

**Data Bit Transmission** (ClockLow/ClockPulse/HoldBit):

[source,systemverilog]
----
ClockLow: begin
  scl_d = 1'b0;
  if (tx_start_stop_i == RepeatedStart && !log_start_q) begin
    sda_d = 1'b1;  // Release for repeated START
  end else begin
    sda_d = shift_reg[bit_index];  // Data bit
  end
end

ClockPulse: begin
  scl_d = 1'b1;
  sda_d = shift_reg[bit_index];  // Stable data
end
----

**ACK/T-bit Decision** (AckLow state, lines 404-427):

[source,systemverilog]
----
AckLow: begin
  scl_d = 1'b0;

  if (tx_is_addr_i && !ibi_mode_i) begin
    // Address byte: release SDA for target ACK
    sda_d = 1'b1;
    internal_sel_od_pp = 1'b0;  // Force OD mode
  end else if (tx_use_tbit_i) begin
    // I3C data write: drive T-bit (odd parity)
    sda_d = !(^shift_reg);
  end else if (ibi_mode_i && ibi_address_byte_i) begin
    // IBI acceptance: controller drives ACK decision
    sda_d = <decision>;  // 0 = accept, 1 = reject
  end else begin
    // Default (I2C data, etc.): release SDA
    sda_d = 1'b1;
  end
end
----

**Data Reception** (ReadClockLow/Pulse/Hold):

[source,systemverilog]
----
ReadClockLow: begin
  scl_d = 1'b0;
  sda_d = 1'b1;  // Always release SDA for target
end

ReadClockPulse: begin
  scl_d = 1'b1;
  sda_d = 1'b1;  // Target drives SDA
  // Sample ctrl_sda_i on scl_i_posedge
end
----

**Abort Read Handling** (ReadTbitPulse, lines 839-847):

[source,systemverilog]
----
ReadTbitPulse: begin
  scl_d = 1'b1;
  if (abort_read_i) begin
    // After a delay, drive SDA low to prevent STOP
    sda_d = 1'b0;  // Force repeated START instead of STOP
  end else begin
    sda_d = 1'b1;  // Normal: release SDA
  end
end
----

=== 6.3 Data Shifting Timing

**TX Path (Load and Transmit):**

1. **Load** (FetchTxData state, line 573):
+
[source,systemverilog]
----
if (state_q == FetchTxData) begin
  load_tx_data = 1'b1;  // shift_reg <= tx_data_i
end
----

2. **Access** (ClockLow/ClockPulse/HoldBit states):
+
[source,systemverilog]
----
sda_d = shift_reg[bit_index];  // bit_index: 7→0
----

3. **Decrement** (HoldBit state, at `tcount_q == 1`):
+
[source,systemverilog]
----
if (state_q == HoldBit && tcount_q == 20'd1) begin
  bit_decr = 1'b1;  // bit_index <= bit_index - 1
end
----

**RX Path (Sample and Shift):**

1. **Clear** (ReadClockLow entry, first bit only):
+
[source,systemverilog]
----
if (state_q == Active && state_d == ReadClockLow) begin
  read_byte_clr = 1'b1;  // read_byte <= 8'h00
end
----

2. **Shift** (ReadClockPulse state, on `scl_i_posedge`, lines 798-802):
+
[source,systemverilog]
----
if (state_q == ReadClockPulse && scl_i_posedge) begin
  shift_data_en = 1'b1;  // read_byte <= {read_byte[6:0], ctrl_sda_i}
end

// Also in ClockPulse for IBI broadcast (lines 678-680):
if (state_q == ClockPulse && scl_i_posedge && ibi_address_byte_i) begin
  shift_data_en = 1'b1;  // Simultaneous TX/RX
end
----

3. **Output** (ReadTbitHold state):
+
[source,systemverilog]
----
if (state_q == ReadTbitHold) begin
  rx_valid_o = 1'b1;      // Pulse
  rx_data_o = read_byte;  // Complete byte
end
----

'''

== Section 7: Transaction Walkthroughs

This section provides step-by-step examples of complete transactions with timing values.

=== 7.1 Complete Write Transaction Example

**Scenario**: Write address 0x7E with START and STOP conditions

**Configuration**:

* System clock: 100 MHz (10 ns period)
* I2C Fast Mode (400 kHz target)
* OD mode timing:
** `t_r_i = 20` (200 ns rise)
** `t_f_i = 20` (200 ns fall)
** `thigh_i = 60` (600 ns high)
** `tlow_i = 130` (1.3 μs low)
** `tsu_sta_i = 60`, `thd_sta_i = 60`, `tsu_sto_i = 60`
** `thd_dat_i = 0`, `t_buf_i = 130`

**Step-by-Step Timeline**:

[cols="1,2,2,2,3", options="header"]
|===
| Step | State | Duration (cycles) | Duration (time) | Actions & Signals

| 1
| **Idle**
| —
| —
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=1`, `host_idle_o=1`. Waiting for transaction.

| 2
| **Active**
| 1
| 10 ns
| `flow_active.sv` asserts: `tx_valid_i=1`, `tx_data_i=0x7E`, `tx_start_stop_i=Start`, `tx_is_addr_i=1`. FSM evaluates: Next = SetupStart.

| 3
| **SetupStart**
| 80
| 800 ns
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=1`. Both lines released. `tcount_d = t_r_i + tsu_sta_i = 20 + 60 = 80`. `log_start_d = 1`.

| 4
| **HoldStart**
| 80
| 800 ns
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=0`. **START condition**: SDA falls while SCL high. `tcount_d = t_f_i + thd_sta_i = 20 + 60 = 80`.

| 5
| **ClockStart**
| 130
| 1.3 μs
| `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=0`. SCL falls, enter clock cycle. `tcount_d = tClockLow = tlow_i - thd_dat_i = 130 - 0 = 130`.

| 6
| **FetchTxData**
| 1
| 10 ns
| `load_tx_data=1` → `shift_reg = 0x7E = 01111110`. `bit_index_clear=1` → `bit_index = 7`. `tcount_d = tNoDelay = 1`.

| 7
| **Active** (2nd)
| 1
| 10 ns
| `log_start_q = 1` (START already done). Next = ClockLow (begin bit transmission).

| 8-15
| **[Bit 7-0 Loop]**
| 8 × 230 = 1840
| 18.4 μs
| For each bit (`bit_index` 7→0): +
  **ClockLow** (130 cycles): `scl_d=0`, `sda_d = shift_reg[bit_index]` +
  **ClockPulse** (80 cycles): `scl_d=1`, `sda_d = shift_reg[bit_index]` (IBI check) +
  **HoldBit** (20 cycles): `scl_d=0`, `sda_d = shift_reg[bit_index]`, `bit_decr=1` at end +
  **Total per bit**: 130 + 80 + 20 = 230 cycles (2.3 μs)

| 16
| **AckLow**
| 130
| 1.3 μs
| `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=1` (release for target ACK). `sample_ack=1` at end. Target pulls SDA low (ACK).

| 17
| **AckPulse**
| 80
| 800 ns
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=1`. `ack_sampled <= ctrl_sda_i = 0` (ACK). `rx_ack_valid_o=1` pulse.

| 18
| **AckHold**
| 20
| 200 ns
| `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=1`. `tx_ready_o=1` pulse. Evaluate `tx_start_stop_i = Stop` → Next = SetupStop.

| 19
| **SetupStop**
| 80
| 800 ns
| `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=0`. Both lines low, prepare for STOP. `tcount_d = t_r_i + tsu_sto_i = 20 + 60 = 80`.

| 20
| **RiseStop**
| 80
| 800 ns
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=0`. SCL rises while SDA low. `tcount_d = tClockPulse = t_r_i + thigh_i = 20 + 60 = 80`.

| 21
| **HoldStop**
| 150
| 1.5 μs
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=1`. **STOP condition**: SDA rises while SCL high. `log_start_d = 0`. `tcount_d = t_r_i + t_buf_i - tsu_sta_i = 20 + 130 - 60 = 90` (note: formula discrepancy, actual uses 150 for bus free). Bus free time.

| 22
| **Idle**
| —
| —
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=1`, `host_idle_o=1`. Transaction complete. Ready for next command.
|===

**Total Transaction Time**:

* START: 800 + 800 + 1300 = 2.9 μs
* Data (8 bits): 18.4 μs
* ACK: 1.3 + 0.8 + 0.2 = 2.3 μs
* STOP: 0.8 + 0.8 + 1.5 = 3.1 μs
* **Total**: ~27.7 μs for 1 address byte

**Effective Bus Speed**: ~36 kHz per byte (well below 400 kHz target, accounting for START/STOP overhead)

=== 7.2 Complete Read Transaction Example

**Scenario**: Read 1 byte with T-bit = 0 (last byte), then STOP

**Configuration**: Same as Write example (100 MHz clock, I2C Fast Mode OD timing)

**Step-by-Step Timeline**:

[cols="1,2,2,2,3", options="header"]
|===
| Step | State | Duration (cycles) | Duration (time) | Actions & Signals

| 1
| **Active**
| 1
| 10 ns
| `flow_active.sv` asserts: `rx_req_i=1`. FSM evaluates: Next = ReadClockLow. `read_byte_clr=1`, `bit_index = 7`.

| 2-9
| **[Bit 7-0 Loop]**
| 8 × 230 = 1840
| 18.4 μs
| For each bit (`bit_index` 7→0): +
  **ReadClockLow** (130 cycles): `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=1` (target sets up bit) +
  **ReadClockPulse** (80 cycles): `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=1`, sample on `scl_i_posedge`, `shift_data_en=1` → `read_byte <= {read_byte[6:0], ctrl_sda_i}` +
  **ReadHoldBit** (20 cycles): `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=1`, `bit_decr=1` at end +
  **Example byte received**: 0x5C = 01011100 +
  **Total per bit**: 230 cycles (2.3 μs)

| 10
| **ReadTbitLow**
| 130
| 1.3 μs
| `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=1` (target drives T-bit). `sample_tbit=1` at end. Target drives T-bit = 0 (last byte, even parity).

| 11
| **ReadTbitPulse**
| 80
| 800 ns
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=1`. `rx_tbit_q <= ctrl_sda_i = 0` (last byte). No `abort_read_i`.

| 12
| **ReadTbitHold**
| 20
| 200 ns
| `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=1`. `rx_valid_o=1`, `rx_data_o = 0x5C`, `rx_data_last_o = !rx_tbit_q = !0 = 1` (TRUE). Since T-bit=0: Next = SetupStop.

| 13
| **SetupStop**
| 80
| 800 ns
| `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=0`. Prepare STOP condition.

| 14
| **RiseStop**
| 80
| 800 ns
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=0`. SCL rises.

| 15
| **HoldStop**
| 150
| 1.5 μs
| `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=1`. **STOP condition**. Bus free time.

| 16
| **Idle**
| —
| —
| Transaction complete. `host_idle_o=1`.
|===

**Total Read Time**:

* Data (8 bits): 18.4 μs
* T-bit: 1.3 + 0.8 + 0.2 = 2.3 μs
* STOP: 0.8 + 0.8 + 1.5 = 3.1 μs
* **Total**: ~23.8 μs for 1 byte read (excluding preceding address phase)

**Alternative Path** (T-bit = 1, more data):

If target drives T-bit = 1 in step 11:

* Step 12: `rx_tbit_q = 1`, `rx_data_last_o = 0` (FALSE)
* Next: FetchTxData → Active → ReadClockLow (continue reading next byte)
* Loop until target signals T-bit = 0

=== 7.3 IBI Transaction Example (Broadcast Case)

**Scenario**: Controller transmits broadcast 0x7E, target responds with IBI, controller accepts

**Step-by-Step Timeline**:

[cols="1,2,3", options="header"]
|===
| Step | State(s) | Actions & Key Events

| 1-5
| START sequence (SetupStart → HoldStart → ClockStart)
| Controller generates START condition. `log_start_q = 1`.

| 6
| FetchTxData
| `shift_reg = 0x7E = 01111110` (broadcast address). `bit_index = 7`.

| 7-8
| ClockLow/ClockPulse (bits 7-6)
| Controller transmits first 2 bits of 0x7E normally.

| 9
| **ClockPulse (bit 5)** — **IBI Detection!**
| • `shift_reg = 0xFC` (internal check, 11111100) +
  • Target pulls SDA different than expected +
  • `ibi_detected_o = (shift_reg == 8'hfc && state_q == ClockPulse) && ctrl_sda_o && !ctrl_sda_i = 1` +
  • **IBI detected!**

| 10
| `flow_active.sv` response
| • Sees `ibi_detected_o = 1` +
  • Asserts `ibi_mode_i = 1` +
  • Asserts `ibi_address_byte_i = 1` +
  • FSM continues in TX states (ClockLow/Pulse/Hold)

| 11-14
| ClockLow/ClockPulse/HoldBit (remaining bits 4-0)
| **Simultaneous TX/RX**: +
  • Controller completes transmitting 0x7E (bits 4→0): `sda_d = shift_reg[bit_index]` +
  • **Special RX logic** (lines 678-680): When `scl_i_posedge && ibi_address_byte_i`, `shift_data_en = 1` +
  • `read_byte <= {read_byte[6:0], ctrl_sda_i}` captures target's IBI address +
  • Example: Target transmits 0x3C = 00111100 +
  • After 8 bits: `shift_reg = 0xFC` (TX done), `read_byte = 0x3C` (RX done)

| 15
| AckLow (9th bit)
| • `scl_d=0`, `sda_d = <controller_decision>` +
  • Logic (lines 404, 449-453): `if (ibi_mode_i && ibi_address_byte_i)` +
  • Controller decides: `sda_d = 0` (ACK, accept IBI) or `sda_d = 1` (NACK, reject) +
  • In this example: **ACK (sda_d = 0)** +
  • `internal_sel_od_pp = 0` (forced OD for ACK)

| 16
| AckPulse
| • `scl_d=1`, `sda_d=0` (controller drives ACK) +
  • `rx_ack_valid_o=1` pulse

| 17
| AckHold
| • `scl_d=0`, `sda_d=1` (release) +
  • `tx_ready_o=1` pulse +
  • `flow_active.sv` sees IBI accepted, prepares for data phase

| 18+
| Transition to PP mode, read IBI data
| • `ibi_address_byte_i = 0` (address phase done) +
  • `internal_sel_od_pp = 1` (switch to PP mode for data) +
  • `flow_active.sv` issues `rx_req_i=1` to read IBI payload +
  • FSM: ReadClockLow → ... (standard RX flow in PP mode) +
  • Target transmits mandatory byte (MDB) and optional data +
  • T-bit = 0 signals end of IBI data

| N
| STOP or continue
| After IBI data complete, controller issues STOP or continues with next command.
|===

**Key Observations**:

* **No FSM state change during IBI**: FSM stays in Write states throughout simultaneous TX/RX
* **Dual-purpose 9th bit**: Uses ACK protocol (not T-bit) for IBI acceptance
* **Mode persistence**: OD mode maintained for IBI broadcast, switches to PP for data phase
* **Special shift enable**: `shift_data_en` triggered in ClockPulse (normally a TX-only state)

'''

== Section 8: Error Handling & Edge Cases

This section documents special cases, error conditions, and recovery mechanisms implemented in the FSM.

=== 8.1 Abort Read Mechanism

The `abort_read_i` signal allows `flow_active.sv` to terminate an ongoing read transaction before the target signals completion (T-bit = 0). This is useful for:

* Flow control (RX FIFO full)
* Protocol violations detected by higher layer
* Timeout conditions
* Preemptive transaction termination

**Implementation** (lines 839-847):

[source,systemverilog]
----
ReadTbitPulse: begin
  scl_d = 1'b1;
  if (abort_read_i) begin
    // Drive SDA low after a delay to prevent STOP condition
    // Forces repeated START instead
    sda_d = 1'b0;
  end else begin
    sda_d = 1'b1;  // Normal: release SDA
  end
end

ReadTbitHold: begin
  scl_d = 1'b0;
  if (abort_read_i) begin
    sda_d = 1'b0;  // Keep SDA low, prevent STOP
    // Next state: FetchTxData → Active (for repeated START)
  end else begin
    // Normal path: evaluate rx_tbit_q for STOP vs continue
  end
end
----

**Abort Timing**:

[source]
----
Normal RX (no abort):
SCL  ____/¯¯¯¯\____    (T-bit pulse)
SDA  ¯¯¯¯¯X¯¯¯¯¯¯¯¯    (X = T-bit value from target)
           ↑
       Sample T-bit
       → Check: T-bit=0? STOP : Continue

Aborted RX (abort_read_i=1):
SCL  ____/¯¯¯¯\____    (T-bit pulse)
SDA  ¯¯¯¯¯X¯¯¯¯\____   (Controller drives low after sampling)
           ↑      ↓
       Sample  Force low
               (prevent STOP, enable repeated START)
----

**State Transitions**:

[cols="2,3,3", options="header"]
|===
| Condition | Normal Path | Aborted Path

| **T-bit = 0** (last byte)
| ReadTbitHold → SetupStop → ... → Idle
| ReadTbitHold → FetchTxData → Active (forced repeated START)

| **T-bit = 1** (more data)
| ReadTbitHold → FetchTxData → Active
| Same (abort has no effect, target already signaling more data)
|===

**Use Case Example**:

1. `flow_active.sv` issues `rx_req_i=1` to read data
2. FSM reads byte successfully, enters ReadTbitPulse
3. `flow_active.sv` detects RX FIFO approaching full
4. `flow_active.sv` asserts `abort_read_i=1`
5. FSM samples T-bit normally, then drives SDA low
6. FSM transitions to FetchTxData (prepares for repeated START or STOP at higher layer's discretion)
7. `flow_active.sv` can issue STOP or continue with different command

=== 8.2 Repeated START Logic

The `log_start_q` flag prevents duplicate START condition generation and enables proper repeated START handling.

**Flag Behavior** (lines 290-298):

[source,systemverilog]
----
logic log_start_q, log_start_d;

always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
  if (!rst_ni) begin
    log_start_q <= 1'b0;
  end else begin
    log_start_q <= log_start_d;
  end
end

// Set in SetupStart state:
log_start_d = 1'b1;  // Mark START in progress

// Cleared in HoldStop state:
log_start_d = 1'b0;  // Mark STOP complete, reset flag
----

**Decision Logic in Active State**:

[cols="2,2,2,3", options="header"]
|===
| `tx_start_stop_i` | `log_start_q` | Decision | Rationale

| `Start` (2)
| 0
| Generate START (→ SetupStart)
| First START of transaction

| `Start` (2)
| 1
| Skip START (→ ClockLow)
| START already generated, avoid duplicate

| `RepeatedStart` (3)
| 0
| Generate START (→ SetupStart)
| Explicit repeated START request

| `RepeatedStart` (3)
| 1
| Generate START (→ SetupStart)
| Force new START even if already started

| `None` (0)
| X
| Continue data (→ ClockLow)
| No bus condition needed

| `Stop` (1)
| X
| Generate STOP (→ SetupStop)
| End transaction
|===

**Repeated START Sequence Example**:

[source]
----
Transaction: Write addr 0x3C, then repeated START, write addr 0x5A

1. Idle → Active (tx_start_stop_i = Start, log_start_q = 0)
2. Active → SetupStart (generate START, log_start_d = 1)
3. ... → ClockLow/Pulse/Hold (transmit 0x3C)
4. ... → AckLow/Pulse/Hold (receive ACK)
5. AckHold → FetchTxData (tx_start_stop_i = RepeatedStart)
6. FetchTxData → Active (load new data 0x5A, log_start_q = 1)
7. Active → SetupStart (tx_start_stop_i = RepeatedStart forces new START)
8. SetupStart → HoldStart → ClockStart (generate repeated START)
9. ... → ClockLow/Pulse/Hold (transmit 0x5A)
10. ... → AckLow/Pulse/Hold → SetupStop → ... → Idle (STOP, log_start_d = 0)
----

**Repeated START SDA Release** (ClockLow state, lines 377-378):

[source,systemverilog]
----
ClockLow: begin
  scl_d = 1'b0;
  if (tx_start_stop_i == RepeatedStart && !log_start_q) begin
    sda_d = 1'b1;  // Release SDA to prepare for START edge
  end else begin
    sda_d = shift_reg[bit_index];  // Normal data bit
  end
end
----

This releases SDA during the SCL low phase immediately before a repeated START, allowing SDA to rise before the START condition (SDA falls while SCL high).

=== 8.3 Timing Edge Cases

==== 8.3.1 Zero or Minimum `tcount_q` Handling

**Minimum Value Clamping** (lines 143-145):

[source,systemverilog]
----
if (host_enable_i && (tcount_q > 20'd1)) begin
  tcount_d = tcount_q - 1'b1;  // Decrement only if > 1
end
// If tcount_q == 20'd1, no decrement → stays at 1
----

**State Transition Trigger**:

All state transitions check `tcount_q == 20'd1`, not `== 0`. This prevents:

* Counter underflow (wrapping to 20'hFFFFF)
* Stuck states (infinite wait at 0)
* Off-by-one timing errors

**Default Case Handling** (lines 125, 140):

[source,systemverilog]
----
unique case (tcount_sel)
  tSetupStart: tcount_d = t_r_i + tsu_sta_i;
  // ... (other cases)
  default:     tcount_d = 20'd1;  // Safety: immediate transition
endcase
----

If an invalid `tcount_sel` value occurs (design error), FSM defaults to `tNoDelay` (1 cycle), allowing recovery rather than lockup.

==== 8.3.2 `host_enable_i` Gating

**Counter Freeze** (line 143):

[source,systemverilog]
----
if (host_enable_i && (tcount_q > 20'd1)) begin
  tcount_d = tcount_q - 1'b1;  // Only decrement when enabled
end
----

When `host_enable_i = 0`:

* `tcount_q` stops decrementing (pauses at current value)
* FSM state does not change (remains in current state)
* SCL/SDA outputs remain at current values
* FSM "freezes" mid-transaction

This enables:

* Debug/test pause capabilities
* Clock gating for power savings (pause FSM during idle periods)
* Synchronization with external events

**Resume Behavior**:

When `host_enable_i` returns to 1:

* `tcount_q` resumes decrementing from paused value
* FSM continues from exact point of pause
* No state corruption or timing glitches

==== 8.3.3 Synchronization Delay Accumulation

**2-Cycle Input Sync** (in `i3c_phy.sv`):

* External SCL/SDA → 2 clock cycles → `ctrl_scl_i` / `ctrl_sda_i`

**Edge Detection Delay** (line 286):

* `scl_i_posedge = !ctrl_scl_i_q && ctrl_scl_i` adds 1 cycle

**Total Latency**: ~3 clock cycles from external event to FSM action

**Impact on Timing**:

This delay is absorbed into the timing parameters:

* `t_r_i` and `t_f_i` account for physical rise/fall times _plus_ input sync delay
* `thigh_i` and `tlow_i` include sync latency in their margins
* External I3C/I2C timing specs are met at the _physical bus_, not at `ctrl_*_i` signals

**Example**:

* I3C spec: `t_SU;STA` ≥ 260 ns (START setup time)
* FSM config: `tsu_sta_i = 26` cycles @ 100 MHz (260 ns)
* Actual bus timing: 260 ns (physical) + 30 ns (3-cycle sync) = 290 ns total (meets spec)

=== 8.4 Bus Collision Detection (IBI)

**Collision Condition** (line 317):

[source,systemverilog]
----
assign ibi_detected_o = (state_q == Idle || (shift_reg == 8'hfc && state_q == ClockPulse))
                        ? ctrl_sda_o && !ctrl_sda_i
                        : 1'b0;
----

**Detection Logic**:

[cols="3,2,3", options="header"]
|===
| Scenario | Condition | Collision Meaning

| **Idle IBI**
| `state_q == Idle && ctrl_sda_o && !ctrl_sda_i`
| Controller releases SDA (expects high), but SDA reads low → Target initiated START

| **Broadcast IBI**
| `shift_reg == 8'hfc && state_q == ClockPulse && ctrl_sda_o && !ctrl_sda_i`
| Controller transmits bit expecting certain value, but SDA differs → Target overriding broadcast

| **Normal Operation**
| Any other state
| No IBI detection logic active
|===

**Case 1: Idle IBI (No True Collision)**

* **Controller state**: Passive, not driving bus
* **Target action**: Initiates START (pulls SDA low)
* **FSM response**: Transition to RX mode, read target address
* **Not a collision**: Target has bus control, controller yields
* **Recovery**: Standard IBI acceptance protocol

**Case 2: Broadcast IBI (True Collision)**

* **Controller state**: Active TX, transmitting 0x7E bit-by-bit
* **Target action**: Drives SDA differently than controller's bit value
* **FSM response**: Continue TX (finish 0x7E), simultaneously RX (read target address)
* **True collision**: Both controller and target driving SDA
* **Resolution**: Special `shift_data_en` logic allows simultaneous operation
* **Arbitration**: I3C protocol defines broadcast 0x7E as "collision-safe" (controller expects target may respond)

**Error Handling Implications**:

* **Idle IBI**: No error, standard IBI protocol flow
* **Broadcast IBI**: Requires careful SDA sampling during TX states (lines 678-680)
* **Unexpected collision** (not during 0x7E): Would manifest as bit errors, handled by higher-layer CRC or parity checks

**Collision-Free Guarantee**:

I3C protocol ensures broadcast address 0x7E is the _only_ scenario where controller and target may both drive SDA:

* All other addresses: Target ACKs via open-drain (controller releases SDA first)
* Data bytes: Either controller TX (target listens) or target TX (controller listens)
* T-bit/ACK: Open-drain protocol prevents drive conflicts

'''

== Section 9: flow_active.sv Integration

This section documents how `i3c_controller_fsm.sv` integrates with the higher-level transaction controller `flow_active.sv`.

=== 9.1 `tx_start_stop_i` Interface

**Enum Definition** (`i3c_pkg.sv`, lines 287-292):

[source,systemverilog]
----
typedef enum logic [1:0] {
  None         = 2'b00,  // No bus condition
  Stop         = 2'b01,  // Generate STOP condition
  Start        = 2'b10,  // Generate START condition (if not already started)
  RepeatedStart = 2'b11  // Generate repeated START (force new START)
} start_stop_e;
----

**Usage Patterns**:

[cols="2,3,3", options="header"]
|===
| `flow_active.sv` State | `tx_start_stop_i` Value | FSM Behavior

| **BroadcastAddr** (first byte)
| `Start`
| Generate START condition (SetupStart → HoldStart → ClockStart), then transmit address byte.

| **TargetAddr** (after broadcast)
| `None`
| Skip START (already generated), go directly to data transmission (ClockLow → ...).

| **WriteData** (middle of write)
| `None`
| Continue transmitting data bytes without bus conditions.

| **WriteData** (last byte)
| `Stop`
| After byte transmission (AckHold), transition to STOP sequence (SetupStop → RiseStop → HoldStop → Idle).

| **PrivateRead** (read after write)
| `RepeatedStart`
| After previous byte's AckHold, generate new START (SetupStart → ...), then send new address with R/W=1.

| **End of Read**
| `Stop` (via T-bit=0)
| FSM detects T-bit=0 from target, automatically transitions to STOP (no explicit `tx_start_stop_i=Stop` needed).
|===

**State-Specific Handling in FSM**:

**Active State Decision** (simplified from lines 560-600):

[source,systemverilog]
----
Active: begin
  if (rx_req_i) begin
    // RX request takes priority
    state_d = ReadClockLow;
  end else if (tx_valid_i) begin
    // TX path
    unique case (tx_start_stop_i)
      Start: begin
        if (!log_start_q) begin
          state_d = SetupStart;  // Generate START
        end else begin
          state_d = ClockLow;    // START already done, skip
        end
      end
      RepeatedStart: begin
        state_d = SetupStart;  // Force new START
      end
      None: begin
        state_d = ClockLow;  // Continue data
      end
      Stop: begin
        state_d = SetupStop;  // Generate STOP
      end
    endcase
  end
end
----

**AckHold State Decision** (simplified from lines 718-735):

[source,systemverilog]
----
AckHold: begin
  tx_ready_o = 1'b1;  // Signal byte complete
  unique case (tx_start_stop_i)
    Stop: begin
      state_d = SetupStop;  // End transaction
    end
    None: begin
      state_d = FetchTxData;  // Get next byte
    end
    RepeatedStart: begin
      state_d = FetchTxData;  // Get next byte (will generate START in Active)
    end
    Start: begin
      state_d = FetchTxData;  // Treat like None (START already done)
    end
  endcase
end
----

=== 9.2 `shift_reg` Interface

**Purpose**: 8-bit TX data holding register for bit-level serialization.

**Load Timing** (FetchTxData state, line 573):

[source,systemverilog]
----
FetchTxData: begin
  load_tx_data = 1'b1;  // shift_reg <= tx_data_i
  bit_index_clear = 1'b1;  // Reset to 7
  tcount_sel = tNoDelay;
  state_d = Active;
end
----

**Access Timing** (ClockLow/ClockPulse/HoldBit states):

[source,systemverilog]
----
ClockLow/ClockPulse/HoldBit: begin
  sda_d = shift_reg[bit_index];  // MSB-first transmission
end
----

**T-bit Calculation** (AckLow state, line 407):

[source,systemverilog]
----
AckLow: begin
  if (tx_use_tbit_i) begin
    sda_d = !(^shift_reg);  // Odd parity of loaded byte
  end
end
----

**Example from `flow_active.sv`**:

[source,systemverilog]
----
// In flow_active.sv (pseudo-code):
state_e state_q;

always_comb begin
  i3c_tx_valid_o = 1'b0;
  i3c_tx_data_o = 8'h00;
  i3c_tx_start_stop_o = None;
  i3c_tx_is_addr_o = 1'b0;

  unique case (state_q)
    BroadcastAddr: begin
      i3c_tx_valid_o = 1'b1;
      i3c_tx_data_o = 8'h7E;  // Broadcast address
      i3c_tx_start_stop_o = Start;  // Generate START
      i3c_tx_is_addr_o = 1'b1;  // Address byte (use OD mode, expect ACK)
    end
    TargetAddr: begin
      i3c_tx_valid_o = 1'b1;
      i3c_tx_data_o = {target_addr, 1'b0};  // 7-bit addr + W bit
      i3c_tx_start_stop_o = None;  // No START (already done)
      i3c_tx_is_addr_o = 1'b1;
    end
    WriteData: begin
      i3c_tx_valid_o = 1'b1;
      i3c_tx_data_o = write_fifo_data;  // Data from FIFO
      i3c_tx_start_stop_o = last_byte ? Stop : None;
      i3c_tx_is_addr_o = 1'b0;  // Data byte (use PP mode if I3C)
      i3c_tx_use_tbit_o = 1'b1;  // Drive T-bit for I3C write
    end
  endcase
end
----

=== 9.3 `read_byte` Interface

**Purpose**: 8-bit RX data accumulation register for bit-level deserialization.

**Clear Timing** (ReadClockLow entry):

[source,systemverilog]
----
// When transitioning from Active to ReadClockLow:
if (state_q == Active && state_d == ReadClockLow) begin
  read_byte_clr = 1'b1;  // read_byte <= 8'h00
end
----

**Shift Timing** (ReadClockPulse state, lines 798-802):

[source,systemverilog]
----
ReadClockPulse: begin
  scl_d = 1'b1;
  sda_d = 1'b1;
  if (scl_i_posedge) begin
    shift_data_en = 1'b1;  // read_byte <= {read_byte[6:0], ctrl_sda_i}
  end
end

// Also for IBI broadcast (ClockPulse state, lines 678-680):
ClockPulse: begin
  if (scl_i_posedge && ibi_address_byte_i) begin
    shift_data_en = 1'b1;  // Simultaneous TX/RX
  end
end
----

**Output Timing** (ReadTbitHold state):

[source,systemverilog]
----
ReadTbitHold: begin
  scl_d = 1'b0;
  sda_d = 1'b1;
  rx_valid_o = 1'b1;  // Pulse for 1 cycle
  rx_data_o = read_byte;  // Complete byte output
  rx_data_last_o = !rx_tbit_q && !ibi_address_byte_i;
end
----

**Example from `flow_active.sv`**:

[source,systemverilog]
----
// In flow_active.sv (pseudo-code):
always_ff @(posedge clk_i) begin
  if (i3c_rx_valid_i) begin
    // Capture received byte
    rx_word_buffer[byte_count] <= i3c_rx_data_i;
    byte_count <= byte_count + 1;

    if (i3c_rx_data_last_i || byte_count == 3) begin
      // Complete 32-bit word or last byte
      rx_fifo_write <= 1'b1;
      rx_fifo_data <= {rx_word_buffer[3:1], i3c_rx_data_i};
      byte_count <= 0;
    end

    if (i3c_rx_data_last_i) begin
      // Target signals end of transfer
      state_d = Idle;  // End read operation
    end else begin
      // Request next byte
      i3c_rx_req_o <= 1'b1;
    end
  end
end
----

=== 9.4 Handshaking Protocol

The FSM and `flow_active.sv` communicate via handshake signals to coordinate byte-level operations.

==== 9.4.1 TX Handshake

[source]
----
flow_active.sv                 FSM
      |                          |
      |  tx_valid_i = 1          |
      |  tx_data_i = 0xAB        |
      |  tx_start_stop_i = None  |
      |  tx_is_addr_i = 0        |
      |─────────────────────────>|
      |                          | FetchTxData: load shift_reg
      |                          | Active → ClockLow
      |                          | (8-bit transmission)
      |                          | ClockLow → ClockPulse → HoldBit (x8)
      |                          | (9th bit ACK/T-bit)
      |                          | AckLow → AckPulse → AckHold
      |                          |
      |      tx_ready_o = 1      | (pulse in AckHold)
      |<─────────────────────────|
      | (byte complete,          |
      |  provide next byte)      |
      |                          |
      |  tx_valid_i = 1 (next)   |
      |─────────────────────────>|
      |                          | (repeat for next byte)
----

**Timing**: `tx_ready_o` pulses for 1 cycle in `AckHold` state (line 714).

==== 9.4.2 RX Handshake

[source]
----
flow_active.sv                 FSM
      |                          |
      |  rx_req_i = 1            |
      |─────────────────────────>|
      |                          | Active → ReadClockLow
      |                          | (8-bit reception)
      |                          | ReadClockLow → ReadClockPulse → ReadHoldBit (x8)
      |                          | (9th bit T-bit)
      |                          | ReadTbitLow → ReadTbitPulse → ReadTbitHold
      |                          |
      |    rx_valid_o = 1        | (pulse in ReadTbitHold)
      |    rx_data_o = 0x5C      |
      |    rx_data_last_o = 0    | (T-bit=1, more data)
      |<─────────────────────────|
      | (capture byte,           |
      |  decide: continue or     |
      |  stop based on T-bit)    |
      |                          |
      |  rx_req_i = 1 (if T=1)   |
      |─────────────────────────>|
      |                          | (repeat for next byte)
----

**Timing**: `rx_valid_o`, `rx_data_o`, `rx_data_last_o` all valid for 1 cycle in `ReadTbitHold` state (line 834).

==== 9.4.3 ACK Handshake

[source]
----
flow_active.sv                 FSM
      |                          |
      | (address byte TX in      |
      |  progress)               |
      |                          | ClockLow → ... → AckLow
      |                          | AckLow: release SDA, prepare to sample
      |                          | AckPulse: sample ctrl_sda_i
      |                          |
      |  rx_ack_valid_o = 1      | (pulse in AckPulse, line 706)
      |  rx_ack_o = 0            | (ACK received)
      |<─────────────────────────|
      | (check ACK status,       |
      |  decide next action)     |
      |                          |
      |      tx_ready_o = 1      | (pulse in AckHold, line 714)
      |<─────────────────────────|
      | (byte complete)          |
----

**Timing**:

* `rx_ack_valid_o` pulses in `AckPulse` when `ack_sampled` is latched
* `rx_ack_o` reflects sampled ACK value (valid when `rx_ack_valid_o=1`)
* `tx_ready_o` pulses in `AckHold` to signal byte transmission complete

=== 9.5 Word Accumulation in flow_active

`flow_active.sv` operates on 32-bit word boundaries (I3C HCI requirement), while the FSM operates on 8-bit bytes. The higher layer accumulates bytes into words:

**Example Accumulation Logic**:

[source,systemverilog]
----
// In flow_active.sv (pseudo-code):
logic [31:0] rx_word_buffer;
logic [1:0]  byte_count;

always_ff @(posedge clk_i) begin
  if (i3c_rx_valid_i) begin
    unique case (byte_count)
      2'd0: rx_word_buffer[7:0]   <= i3c_rx_data_i;
      2'd1: rx_word_buffer[15:8]  <= i3c_rx_data_i;
      2'd2: rx_word_buffer[23:16] <= i3c_rx_data_i;
      2'd3: rx_word_buffer[31:24] <= i3c_rx_data_i;
    endcase

    byte_count <= byte_count + 1;

    if (byte_count == 2'd3 || i3c_rx_data_last_i) begin
      // Write complete word to RX FIFO
      rx_fifo_write <= 1'b1;
      rx_fifo_data  <= {rx_word_buffer[31:8], i3c_rx_data_i};
      byte_count    <= 2'd0;
    end
  end
end
----

**Partial Word Handling**:

If `rx_data_last_o=1` before 4 bytes received (e.g., after 2 bytes):

* `flow_active.sv` writes partial word to FIFO with valid byte count metadata
* Higher software layer (I3C HCI driver) interprets partial word based on transfer descriptor

'''

== Section 10: Mode Selection Deep Dive

This section provides detailed analysis of OD vs PP mode switching logic and timing profile selection.

=== 10.1 OD vs PP Timing Selection

**Core Selection Logic** (line 336):

[source,systemverilog]
----
assign internal_sel_od_pp = ~tx_is_addr_i && (!ibi_address_byte_i);
----

**Expanded Truth Table with Examples**:

[cols="2,1,1,1,2,2,2", options="header"]
|===
| Scenario | `tx_is_addr_i` | `ibi_address_byte_i` | `internal_sel_od_pp` | Mode | Timing Set | Rationale

| **I3C Address (7-bit + R/W)**
| 1
| 0
| 0
| OD
| `t_r_i`, `tlow_i`, `thigh_i`, ...
| I3C spec requires address phase in OD for ACK compatibility and multi-master arbitration

| **IBI Broadcast (8'h7E)**
| 0
| 1
| 0
| OD
| `t_r_i`, `tlow_i`, `thigh_i`, ...
| Broadcast address uses OD to enable target collision detection (IBI mechanism)

| **I3C Data Write**
| 0
| 0
| 1
| PP
| `t_r_pp_i`, `tlow_pp_i`, `thigh_pp_i`, ...
| I3C SDR data phase uses PP for higher speed (up to 12.5 MHz typical)

| **I3C Data Read**
| 0
| 0
| 1
| PP
| `t_r_pp_i`, `tlow_pp_i`, `thigh_pp_i`, ...
| I3C SDR read uses PP during data bits; T-bit uses OD (special handling at lines 496, 506, 527, 540)

| **I2C Address**
| 1
| 0
| 0
| OD
| `t_r_i`, `tlow_i`, `thigh_i`, ...
| I2C always uses OD mode (PP mode parameters ignored)

| **I2C Data**
| 0
| 0
| 1
| "PP"
| `t_r_pp_i`, `tlow_pp_i`, `thigh_pp_i`, ...
| For I2C devices, `t_r_pp_i == t_r_i` and `tlow_pp_i == tlow_i` (same timing, different registers)
|===

**Special Case: T-bit Reception OD Override** (lines 496, 506, 527, 540):

During I3C read T-bit sampling, FSM forces OD mode even though `internal_sel_od_pp` computes to PP:

[source,systemverilog]
----
// Line 496 (ReadTbitLow state):
internal_sel_od_pp = 1'b0;  // Force OD mode for T-bit

// Line 506 (ReadTbitPulse state):
internal_sel_od_pp = 1'b0;  // Maintain OD mode

// Line 527 (ReadTbitHold state):
internal_sel_od_pp = 1'b0;  // Hold OD mode
----

**Rationale**: Target drives T-bit using OD protocol (pulls low for 0, releases for 1), so controller must use OD timing to properly sample.

=== 10.2 Timing Profile Switching

**Atomic Mode Change** (lines 109-146):

[source,systemverilog]
----
always_comb begin : counter_functions
  tcount_d = tcount_q;
  if (load_tcount) begin
    if (internal_sel_od_pp == 1'b0) begin
      // Load OD timing based on tcount_sel
      unique case (tcount_sel)
        tSetupStart: tcount_d = t_r_i + tsu_sta_i;
        // ...
      endcase
    end else begin
      // Load PP timing based on tcount_sel
      unique case (tcount_sel)
        tSetupStart: tcount_d = t_r_pp_i + t_cbsr_i;
        // ...
      endcase
    end
  end else if (host_enable_i && (tcount_q > 20'd1)) begin
    tcount_d = tcount_q - 1'b1;  // Decrement
  end
end
----

**Mode Switch Timing**:

1. **State Transition**: Current state completes (tcount_q reaches 1)
2. **Next State Entry**: New state becomes active
3. **load_tcount = 1**: Triggered in new state's entry logic
4. **Mode Evaluation**: `internal_sel_od_pp` computed based on current TX/RX context
5. **Timing Load**: Appropriate timing formula selected (OD or PP) based on mode
6. **Counter Start**: `tcount_q` loads new value, begins decrementing

**Example: Address (OD) to Data (PP) Transition**:

[source]
----
State: HoldBit (last bit of address byte 0x3C)
  • internal_sel_od_pp = 0 (address byte, OD mode)
  • tcount_q = 1 (about to transition)

State: AckLow (9th bit, address ACK)
  • internal_sel_od_pp = 0 (still OD for ACK)
  • load_tcount = 1, tcount_sel = tClockLow
  • tcount_d = tlow_i - thd_dat_i (OD formula)

State: AckPulse → AckHold (ACK complete)
  • internal_sel_od_pp = 0 (maintain OD)

State: FetchTxData (load next byte 0xAB, data byte)
  • tx_is_addr_i = 0 (data byte), ibi_address_byte_i = 0
  • internal_sel_od_pp = 1 (switch to PP!)
  • load_tx_data = 1, shift_reg <= 0xAB

State: ClockLow (first bit of data byte)
  • internal_sel_od_pp = 1 (PP mode)
  • load_tcount = 1, tcount_sel = tClockLow
  • tcount_d = tlow_pp_i - thd_pp_i (PP formula)
  • Mode switch complete!
----

**No Glitches**:

* Mode switch occurs during state transition (no mid-state change)
* `tcount_d` assignment is combinational (atomic in same cycle as mode evaluation)
* `tcount_q` register update happens on clock edge (synchronized)
* SCL/SDA outputs controlled by state machine (stable during transitions)

=== 10.3 `sel_od_pp_o` Output

**Purpose**: Controls physical layer (`i3c_phy.sv`) output driver mode.

**Assignment** (line 339):

[source,systemverilog]
----
// In state_outputs block:
sel_od_pp_o = internal_sel_od_pp;
----

**Physical Layer Interpretation** (in `i3c_phy.sv`):

[source,systemverilog]
----
// Pseudo-code from i3c_phy.sv:
always_comb begin
  if (sel_od_pp_i == 1'b0) begin
    // Open-Drain mode
    pad_scl_oe = ctrl_scl_i ? 1'b0 : 1'b1;  // OE=1 when pulling low
    pad_scl_out = 1'b0;  // Always drive low (pull-up provides high)
    pad_sda_oe = ctrl_sda_i ? 1'b0 : 1'b1;
    pad_sda_out = 1'b0;
  end else begin
    // Push-Pull mode
    pad_scl_oe = 1'b1;  // Always enabled
    pad_scl_out = ctrl_scl_i;  // Actively drive both 0 and 1
    pad_sda_oe = 1'b1;
    pad_sda_out = ctrl_sda_i;
  end
end
----

**Timing Requirement**:

`sel_od_pp_o` must be stable _before_ SCL/SDA transitions occur:

* FSM guarantees this by setting mode in state entry logic
* State entry occurs on clock edge (registered)
* SCL/SDA outputs derived from state (`scl_d`, `sda_d` in state_outputs block)
* Both mode and bus signals update on same clock edge → no race condition

**Special Handling During RX**:

Even though `internal_sel_od_pp = 1` (PP mode) during I3C data reads, the FSM releases SDA (`sda_d = 1`), allowing target to drive. The physical layer sees:

* `sel_od_pp_o = 1` (PP mode)
* `ctrl_sda_o = 1` (release)
* Physical driver: `pad_sda_oe = 1`, `pad_sda_out = 1` (drives high weakly or releases depending on PHY implementation)

Target overrides with stronger drive, controller samples via `ctrl_sda_i`.

'''

== Section 11: Implementation Notes

This section documents internal implementation details, register organization, and safety mechanisms.

=== 11.1 Internal Registers

The FSM maintains 9 primary internal registers (all synchronous to `clk_i`, reset by `rst_ni`):

[cols="2,1,3,2,2", options="header"]
|===
| Register | Width | Purpose | Reset Value | Update Logic

| **`state_q`**
| 5 bits
| Current FSM state (one of 20 states)
| `Idle`
| `state_q <= state_d` on clock edge

| **`tcount_q`**
| 20 bits
| Timing counter (down-counter)
| `20'd1`
| Decrements each cycle (if `host_enable_i` and `> 1`), or loads new value on `load_tcount`

| **`bit_index`**
| 3 bits
| Bit position counter (7→0 for 8 bits)
| `3'd7`
| Decrements on `bit_decr` (after each bit TX/RX), resets to 7 on `bit_index_clear`

| **`shift_reg`**
| 8 bits
| TX shift register (holds outgoing byte)
| `8'h00`
| Loads from `tx_data_i` on `load_tx_data`, static during transmission

| **`read_byte`**
| 8 bits
| RX shift register (accumulates incoming byte)
| `8'h00`
| Clears on `read_byte_clr`, shifts in bits on `shift_data_en`

| **`ack_sampled`**
| 1 bit
| Latched ACK value from target
| `1'b1` (NACK)
| Captures `ctrl_sda_i` on `sample_ack` pulse (AckLow→AckPulse)

| **`rx_tbit_q`**
| 1 bit
| Latched T-bit value from target
| `1'b1` (more data)
| Captures `ctrl_sda_i` on `sample_tbit` pulse (ReadTbitLow→ReadTbitPulse)

| **`log_start_q`**
| 1 bit
| START condition flag (prevents duplicate START)
| `1'b0`
| Set to 1 in SetupStart, cleared to 0 in HoldStop

| **`ctrl_scl_i_q`**
| 1 bit
| Previous cycle's SCL value (for edge detection)
| `1'b1`
| `ctrl_scl_i_q <= ctrl_scl_i` on each clock edge

| **`sda_q`** ^[1]^
| 1 bit
| Previous cycle's SDA output (for glitch prevention)
| `1'b1`
| `sda_q <= sda_d` on each clock edge
|===

^[1]^ **Note**: `sda_q` is used in Active state to hold SDA at previous value during state transitions, preventing glitches (line 350).

**Total Register Bit Count**: 5 + 20 + 3 + 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = **49 bits**

=== 11.2 SCL/SDA Input Synchronization

**Synchronization Path** (in `i3c_phy.sv`):

[source,systemverilog]
----
// Physical I3C pads
input  wire pad_scl_i,
input  wire pad_sda_i,

// 2-stage synchronizer (caliptra_prim_flop_2sync instance)
logic scl_synced, sda_synced;

caliptra_prim_flop_2sync #(.Width(1)) u_scl_sync (
  .clk_i  (clk_i),
  .rst_ni (rst_ni),
  .d_i    (pad_scl_i),
  .q_o    (scl_synced)
);

caliptra_prim_flop_2sync #(.Width(1)) u_sda_sync (
  .clk_i  (clk_i),
  .rst_ni (rst_ni),
  .d_i    (pad_sda_i),
  .q_o    (sda_synced)
);

// Output to FSM
assign ctrl_scl_i = scl_synced;
assign ctrl_sda_i = sda_synced;
----

**2-Stage Synchronizer Implementation**:

[source,systemverilog]
----
// Internal to caliptra_prim_flop_2sync module:
logic sync_stage1, sync_stage2;

always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
  if (!rst_ni) begin
    sync_stage1 <= 1'b1;  // Reset to idle (high)
    sync_stage2 <= 1'b1;
  end else begin
    sync_stage1 <= d_i;      // First synchronization stage
    sync_stage2 <= sync_stage1;  // Second synchronization stage
  end
end

assign q_o = sync_stage2;  // Output after 2 cycles
----

**Timing Impact**:

* **Delay**: 2 clock cycles from `pad_*_i` to `ctrl_*_i`
* **Metastability Protection**: Reduces probability of metastable state to ~10^-12^ (assuming proper design)
* **Glitch Filtering**: Short glitches (<2 clock periods) on pads may be filtered

**Edge Detection** (line 286):

[source,systemverilog]
----
logic ctrl_scl_i_q;  // Previous cycle's synchronized SCL

always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
  if (!rst_ni) ctrl_scl_i_q <= 1'b1;
  else         ctrl_scl_i_q <= ctrl_scl_i;
end

// Rising edge detection
assign scl_i_posedge = !ctrl_scl_i_q && ctrl_scl_i;

// scl_i_posedge = 1 for exactly 1 cycle when SCL transitions 0→1
----

**Total Latency from External Event to FSM Action**:

1. External SCL/SDA transition
2. 2 cycles: Synchronization (`pad_*_i` → `ctrl_*_i`)
3. 1 cycle: Edge detection register (`ctrl_scl_i` → `ctrl_scl_i_q`, compare)
4. **Total**: ~3 clock cycles

This latency is accounted for in timing parameter selection (embedded in `t_r_i`, `t_f_i`, etc.).

=== 11.3 State Safety Mechanisms

The FSM implements several safety features to prevent lockup and ensure robust operation.

==== 11.3.1 Default State Handling

All state transition logic uses `unique case` or `priority case` statements with explicit defaults:

[source,systemverilog]
----
// State transition logic (lines 560-867):
unique case (state_q)
  Idle: begin
    // ... state logic
  end
  Active: begin
    // ... state logic
  end
  // ... (all 20 states)
  default: begin
    // Safety: return to Idle on unknown state
    state_d = Idle;
    scl_d = 1'b1;
    sda_d = 1'b1;
  end
endcase
----

**Rationale**:

* If state register corrupts (e.g., SEU, glitch), FSM recovers to safe Idle state
* Prevents infinite loop in undefined state
* Releases bus (SCL/SDA high) to avoid blocking I3C bus

==== 11.3.2 Counter Minimum Clamping

Timing counter cannot decrement below 1:

[source,systemverilog]
----
if (host_enable_i && (tcount_q > 20'd1)) begin
  tcount_d = tcount_q - 1'b1;
end
// If tcount_q == 20'd1, no decrement (stays at 1)
----

**Rationale**:

* Prevents underflow (20'd1 - 1 = 20'd0, but check prevents this)
* State transitions trigger on `tcount_q == 20'd1`, not `== 0`
* If counter stuck at 1, FSM transitions immediately (recovers from timing errors)

==== 11.3.3 Bit Index Bounds

Bit index counter operates in range [0, 7]:

[source,systemverilog]
----
logic [2:0] bit_index;  // 3 bits: 0-7 range

// Reset/clear to 7 (MSB first)
if (bit_index_clear) bit_index <= 3'd7;

// Decrement after each bit
if (bit_decr) bit_index <= bit_index - 1'b1;

// State logic checks bit_index == 0 to transition to ACK/T-bit states
----

**Bounds Checking**:

* Decrement occurs in HoldBit/ReadHoldBit states (8 times per byte)
* After 8 decrements: `bit_index` goes 7→6→...→1→0
* At `bit_index == 0`, FSM transitions to AckLow/ReadTbitLow (no further decrements)
* No explicit underflow check needed (3-bit value wraps to 7 if decremented from 0, but logic prevents this)

==== 11.3.4 Reset Behavior

All registers have defined reset values:

[source,systemverilog]
----
always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
  if (!rst_ni) begin
    state_q       <= Idle;        // Safe idle state
    tcount_q      <= 20'd1;       // Immediate transition value
    bit_index     <= 3'd7;        // MSB first
    shift_reg     <= 8'h00;       // Empty
    read_byte     <= 8'h00;       // Empty
    ack_sampled   <= 1'b1;        // NACK (safe default)
    rx_tbit_q     <= 1'b1;        // More data (safe default)
    log_start_q   <= 1'b0;        // No START in progress
    ctrl_scl_i_q  <= 1'b1;        // Bus idle
    sda_q         <= 1'b1;        // Bus idle
  end else begin
    // Normal operation
  end
end
----

**Reset Assertion Duration**:

* `rst_ni` should be held low for ≥2 clock cycles to ensure all synchronizers reset
* Release `rst_ni` synchronous to `clk_i` rising edge (recommended)

'''

== Section 12: References & Appendices

=== 12.1 I3C Specification References

This FSM implements timing and protocol requirements from the following specifications:

==== MIPI I3C Basic Specification v1.1.1

**Document**: MIPI Alliance Specification for I3C℠ Basic +
**Version**: v1.1.1 (Errata 01, 11.03.2022) +
**Publisher**: MIPI Alliance, Inc.

**Referenced Sections**:

* **Section 5.1.2.3.1 - Open-Drain ACK Timing**
** Address byte 9th bit protocol
** Target ACK/NACK signaling via open-drain SDA
** Setup and hold time requirements for ACK sampling
** Implementation: FSM `AckLow`, `AckPulse`, `AckHold` states (lines 704-735)

* **Section 5.1.2.3.4 - T-bit (Transition Bit) Timing**
** I3C SDR data byte 9th bit protocol
** Target-driven flow control mechanism (T-bit = 0: last byte, T-bit = 1: more data)
** Odd parity calculation: `T-bit = !(XOR of byte)`
** Implementation: FSM `ReadTbitLow`, `ReadTbitPulse`, `ReadTbitHold` states (lines 816-867); TX T-bit calculation (line 407)

* **Section 5.1.6 - In-Band Interrupts (IBI)**
** Target-initiated interrupt mechanism
** IBI detection via bus collision (START from target when bus idle, or during broadcast 8'h7E)
** IBI address exchange and acceptance protocol (ACK to accept, NACK to reject)
** Implementation: IBI detection logic (line 317); broadcast IBI special handling (lines 678-680, 404, 449-453)

* **Section 5.2.1.3 - Open-Drain vs Push-Pull Phases**
** I3C mixed-mode signaling: OD for address, PP for data
** Timing requirements for mode transitions
** Implementation: `internal_sel_od_pp` selection logic (line 336); timing counter mode switching (lines 112-142)

==== MIPI I3C Host Controller Interface (HCI) Specification v1.2

**Document**: MIPI Alliance Specification for I3C℠ HCI +
**Version**: v1.2 +
**Publisher**: MIPI Alliance, Inc.

**Referenced Sections**:

* **Section 8.1.2 - Dynamic Address Parity**
** 7-bit dynamic address + parity bit = 8-bit address byte
** Used in I3C address assignment and device identification
** Not directly implemented in FSM (handled by `flow_active.sv`), but FSM transmits/receives these address bytes

=== 12.2 Related Modules

This FSM integrates with the following modules in the I3C controller implementation:

==== flow_active.sv

**Location**: `src/ctrl/flow_active.sv` +
**Purpose**: Transaction-level controller, orchestrates I3C/I2C transfers

**Interface**:

* **Provides to FSM**: `tx_valid_i`, `tx_data_i`, `tx_start_stop_i`, `tx_is_addr_i`, `tx_use_tbit_i`, `rx_req_i`, `ibi_mode_i`, `ibi_address_byte_i`, `abort_read_i`
* **Receives from FSM**: `tx_ready_o`, `rx_ack_o`, `rx_ack_valid_o`, `rx_valid_o`, `rx_data_o`, `rx_data_last_o`, `ibi_detected_o`, `host_idle_o`

**Responsibilities**:

* Parse I3C HCI command descriptors
* Generate START/STOP/repeated START sequences
* Accumulate 8-bit bytes into 32-bit words (RX FIFO write)
* Handle CCC (Common Command Code) encoding
* Manage IBI acceptance policy
* Report transfer status to HCI software layer

==== i3c_phy.sv

**Location**: `src/ctrl/i3c_phy.sv` +
**Purpose**: Physical layer (PHY) interface to I3C bus pads

**Functions**:

* **Input Synchronization**: 2-stage synchronizers for `pad_scl_i` and `pad_sda_i` (metastability protection)
* **Output Drivers**: OD vs PP mode multiplexing based on `sel_od_pp_i` from FSM
* **Pad Control**: Drives `pad_scl_oe`, `pad_scl_out`, `pad_sda_oe`, `pad_sda_out` to physical pads

**Interface with FSM**:

* **From FSM**: `ctrl_scl_o`, `ctrl_sda_o`, `sel_od_pp_o`
* **To FSM**: `ctrl_scl_i`, `ctrl_sda_i` (synchronized inputs)

==== controller_pkg.sv

**Location**: `src/ctrl/controller_pkg.sv` +
**Purpose**: Package definitions for controller subsystem

**Contents**:

* Type definitions for controller-specific structures
* Constants for buffer sizes, FIFO depths
* Helper functions for bit manipulation

==== i3c_pkg.sv

**Location**: `src/i3c_pkg.sv` +
**Purpose**: I3C-specific type definitions and constants

**Contents**:

* `start_stop_e` enum (lines 287-292): `None`, `Stop`, `Start`, `RepeatedStart`
* I3C command codes (CCC definitions)
* I3C device characteristic registers (DCR, BCR)
* Timing parameter structures

=== 12.4 Acronyms & Glossary

==== Acronyms

[cols="1,4", options="header"]
|===
| Acronym | Expansion

| **ACK** | Acknowledge - 9th bit signal (0 = acknowledge, 1 = not acknowledge)
| **BCR** | Bus Characteristic Register (I3C device capability register)
| **CCC** | Common Command Code (I3C broadcast/direct commands)
| **CSR** | Control and Status Register
| **DAA** | Dynamic Address Assignment (I3C enumeration process)
| **DCR** | Device Characteristic Register (I3C device type identifier)
| **FSM** | Finite State Machine
| **HCI** | Host Controller Interface (I3C software-hardware interface spec)
| **IBI** | In-Band Interrupt (target-initiated interrupt mechanism, I3C-specific)
| **MDB** | Mandatory Data Byte (first byte of IBI payload, contains interrupt details)
| **MSB** | Most Significant Bit (transmitted first in I3C/I2C)
| **NACK** | Not Acknowledge - 9th bit signal (SDA high during ACK bit)
| **OD** | Open-Drain - bus driver can only pull low, not drive high (passive pull-up provides high)
| **PP** | Push-Pull - bus driver can actively drive both high and low levels
| **PHY** | Physical Layer (hardware interface to bus pads)
| **SDR** | Single Data Rate - standard I3C transfer mode (as opposed to HDR modes)
| **SEU** | Single Event Upset (transient fault from radiation or noise)
| **T-bit** | Transition Bit - I3C 9th bit for end-of-data indication (0 = last, 1 = more)
| **TCRI** | Test and Control Requirement Interface (I3C test mode specification)
|===

==== Glossary of Terms

[cols="2,5", options="header"]
|===
| Term | Definition

| **Address Phase**
| Portion of I3C/I2C transfer where 7-bit address + R/W bit is transmitted. Always uses open-drain signaling in I3C. 9th bit is ACK (not T-bit).

| **Bit-level Serialization**
| Process of transmitting an 8-bit byte MSB-first over SDA, one bit per clock cycle. Handled by FSM states ClockLow → ClockPulse → HoldBit (repeated 8 times).

| **Broadcast Address**
| I3C address 8'h7E (0111111 + R/W bit) used for CCC commands and IBI detection. All targets listen to this address.

| **Bus Condition**
| START, repeated START, or STOP condition on I3C/I2C bus (SDA transition while SCL high).

| **Bus Free Time**
| Minimum duration both SCL and SDA must remain high after STOP before next START. I2C Fast Mode: ≥1.3 μs. I3C: ≥160 ns.

| **Clock Stretching**
| I2C feature where target holds SCL low to pause transfer (not supported by this FSM; I3C SDR mode does not use clock stretching).

| **Controller**
| I3C/I2C bus master device that generates clock (SCL) and initiates transfers. Formerly called "master" in I2C terminology.

| **Data Phase**
| Portion of I3C transfer after address phase where data bytes are transmitted or received. I3C SDR data phase uses push-pull signaling. 9th bit is T-bit (not ACK).

| **Dynamic Address**
| 7-bit I3C address assigned by controller during DAA (ENTDAA CCC). Includes parity bit for error detection.

| **Edge Detection**
| Logic to identify SCL/SDA transitions (0→1 or 1→0). Implemented via previous-cycle comparison: `scl_i_posedge = !ctrl_scl_i_q && ctrl_scl_i`.

| **Flow Control**
| Mechanism to pause or terminate transfers. I3C uses T-bit (target-driven) and `abort_read_i` (controller-driven).

| **Handshake**
| Coordinated signal exchange between FSM and `flow_active.sv` to transfer byte-level data (e.g., `tx_valid_i` → FSM processes → `tx_ready_o` pulse).

| **Hot-Join**
| I3C feature where a new target can request enumeration while bus is active (uses IBI mechanism with specific address).

| **Metastability**
| Unstable state of a flip-flop when input changes near clock edge. 2-stage synchronizers reduce probability to negligible levels (~10^-12^).

| **Odd Parity**
| T-bit calculation method: XOR all 8 bits, invert result. Even number of 1's → T-bit=1. Odd number of 1's → T-bit=0.

| **Open-Drain Signaling**
| Electrical scheme where driver can only pull signal low (0). Passive pull-up resistor provides high (1) level. Allows wired-AND bus arbitration.

| **Push-Pull Signaling**
| Electrical scheme where driver actively drives both low (0) and high (1) levels. Faster transitions than open-drain, but no wired-AND capability.

| **Repeated START**
| START condition generated without preceding STOP. Used to change direction (write→read) or address different target without releasing bus.

| **Rising Edge**
| 0→1 transition of a signal (e.g., SCL rising edge). I3C/I2C specs require SDA sampling on SCL rising edge.

| **Sample Point**
| Instant when SDA is captured by receiver. For I3C: SCL rising edge (FSM uses `scl_i_posedge` for timing).

| **Setup Time**
| Minimum duration a signal must be stable _before_ a clock edge (e.g., SDA stable before SCL rises).

| **Hold Time**
| Minimum duration a signal must remain stable _after_ a clock edge (e.g., SDA stable after SCL rises).

| **Shift Register**
| Register that shifts its contents left or right each cycle. TX `shift_reg` shifts data out MSB-first. RX `read_byte` shifts data in MSB-first.

| **Synchronizer**
| Multi-stage flip-flop chain to safely transfer async signals into clock domain. 2-stage synchronizer: reduces metastability probability to ~10^-12^.

| **Target**
| I3C/I2C bus slave device addressed by controller. Responds to commands, may drive SDA during data phase or IBI. Formerly called "slave" in I2C terminology.

| **Timing Counter**
| 20-bit down-counter (`tcount_q`) that implements delay periods between FSM states. Loads value based on timing profile (OD or PP mode), decrements each cycle.

| **Timing Profile**
| Set of 10 timing parameters (tSetupStart, tHoldStart, ..., tNoDelay) calculated from CSR values. Separate formulas for OD and PP modes.

| **Transaction**
| Complete I3C/I2C transfer: START + address + data bytes + STOP. May include repeated START for direction change.

| **Tri-state**
| Output driver with three states: drive low (0), drive high (1), high-impedance (Z). Open-drain uses low/Z. Push-pull uses low/high.
|===

[cols="1,2,1", options="header"]

| State | Function | Typical Duration (I2C Fast Mode)

| Idle | Bus idle, waiting | —
| Active | Transaction decision | 10 ns
| FetchTxData | Load TX byte | 10 ns
| SetupStart | START setup | 800 ns
| HoldStart | START condition | 800 ns
| ClockStart | SCL low after START | 1.3 μs
| ClockLow | Data bit setup | 1.3 μs (per bit)
| ClockPulse | Data bit valid | 800 ns (per bit)
| HoldBit | Data bit hold | 200 ns (per bit)
| AckLow | ACK/T-bit setup | 1.3 μs
| AckPulse | ACK/T-bit sample | 800 ns
| AckHold | Byte complete | 200 ns
| SetupStop | STOP setup | 800 ns
| RiseStop | SCL rises for STOP | 800 ns
| HoldStop | Bus free time | 1.5 μs
| ReadClockLow | RX bit setup | 1.3 μs (per bit)
| ReadClockPulse | RX bit sample | 800 ns (per bit)
| ReadHoldBit | RX bit hold | 200 ns (per bit)
| ReadTbitLow | T-bit setup | 1.3 μs
| ReadTbitPulse | T-bit sample | 800 ns
| ReadTbitHold | RX byte complete | 200 ns
|===

=== A.2 Timing Parameters Quick Reference

[cols="2,2,2,2", options="header"]
|===
| Parameter | OD Formula | PP Formula | Typical Value (I2C @ 100 MHz)

| tSetupStart | `t_r + tsu_sta` | `t_r_pp + t_cbsr` | 80 cycles (800 ns)
| tHoldStart | `t_f + thd_sta` | `t_f_pp + t_casr` | 80 cycles (800 ns)
| tClockLow | `tlow - thd_dat` | `tlow_pp - thd_pp` | 130 cycles (1.3 μs)
| tClockPulse | `t_r + thigh` | `t_r_pp + thigh_pp` | 80 cycles (800 ns)
| tHoldBit | `t_f + thd_dat` | `t_f_pp + thd_pp` | 20 cycles (200 ns)
| tSetupStop | `t_r + tsu_sto` | `t_r_pp + t_casr` | 80 cycles (800 ns)
| tHoldStop | `t_r + t_buf - tsu_sta` | Same (uses OD `t_buf`) | 150 cycles (1.5 μs)
|===

[cols="2,1,4", options="header"]
|===
| Signal Group | Direction | Key Signals

| Bus Interface | I/O | `ctrl_scl_i`, `ctrl_scl_o`, `ctrl_sda_i`, `ctrl_sda_o`
| Timing (OD) | Input | `t_r_i`, `t_f_i`, `thigh_i`, `tlow_i`, `tsu_sta_i`, `thd_sta_i`, `tsu_sto_i`, `thd_dat_i`, `t_buf_i`, `tsu_dat_i`
| Timing (PP) | Input | `t_r_pp_i`, `t_f_pp_i`, `thigh_pp_i`, `tlow_pp_i`, `tsu_pp_i`, `thd_pp_i`, `t_casr_i`, `t_cbsr_i`
| TX Control | Input | `tx_valid_i`, `tx_data_i`, `tx_start_stop_i`, `tx_is_addr_i`, `tx_use_tbit_i`
| TX Status | Output | `tx_ready_o`, `rx_ack_o`, `rx_ack_valid_o`
| RX Control | Input | `rx_req_i`
| RX Status | Output | `rx_valid_o`, `rx_data_o`, `rx_data_last_o`
| IBI | I/O | `ibi_detected_o`, `ibi_mode_i`, `ibi_address_byte_i`, `abort_read_i`
| Mode Select | Output | `sel_od_pp_o`
